title: Reading the fine print
description: The small text is where prices change — a five-minute guide to spotting what matters.

body.heading: What to hunt for
paragraphs: In any offer, look for four things: the total price including fees, how long the price lasts, what happens when an introductory period ends, and how you cancel. Those four answers reveal most surprises in advance.
Watch for words like 'from', 'up to', and 'introductory'. They usually mean the headline price is the best case, temporary, or both.

body.heading: Contracts and commitments
paragraphs: Check the minimum term and any early-exit charges before signing. A cheap monthly price tied to a long contract can cost far more than a flexible option if your life changes.
If you cannot find a clear answer, ask the seller directly and keep their reply. A trustworthy seller explains terms plainly; pressure to sign quickly is itself information.

body.heading: Slow is smart
paragraphs: Fine print rewards the unhurried. Reading for five minutes before you commit is one of the highest-paid activities in everyday money life.

takeaway: In any offer, find the total price, how long it lasts, what happens next, and how to cancel.
